Visitors will experience the established capabilities that have made Actus X a trusted solution worldwide – compliance logging, QA and technical monitoring, browser-based multiviewing, clip creation and AI-powered media intelligence – alongside major advances in usability, performance, scalability and integration.

As media operations expand across linear, OTT and digital platforms, broadcasters must monitor more channels, formats and delivery points, often with distributed teams and shifting requirements. The latest evolution of Actus X addresses this through workflow-focused user experiences, intelligent automation, flexible deployment and deeper integration across the LiveU EcoSystem.

"Broadcast operations are becoming more dynamic, distributed and complex, but the technology supporting them should become simpler," said Sima Levy, CEO of Actus Digital. "The next generation of Actus X is designed around the people who use it every day, giving each team the visibility, flexibility and intelligence it needs to work faster and make better decisions."

Rebuilt for Dynamic Operations

The new Actus X infrastructure has been rebuilt using advanced software technologies for faster performance, greater scalability and enhanced cloud efficiency. System configuration is now significantly more dynamic: as a channel changes resolution, a new service launches or additional capacity is needed, adjustments can be made quickly without complex engineering work. This flexibility is especially valuable for temporary services, live events and fast changing broadcast environments.

A Next-Generation Browser-Based Multiviewer

Actus will also showcase its next-generation browser-based multiviewer, built for distributed, personalized monitoring. Each user can create unlimited layouts via drag-and-drop, selecting the channels, alerts and technical information relevant to their role – no longer restricted to fixed layouts or dedicated monitoring stations. Because it runs entirely within a browser, it can be securely accessed from virtually anywhere, with sub-second latency for real-time monitoring.

The experience goes beyond passive viewing. Operators can listen to live audio, rewind content instantly, investigate alerts and interact directly with monitored streams, all from one interface, with integrated alerts enabling faster response and less manual supervision.

Cloud-Optimized Without Compromising Choice

Actus has invested extensively in optimizing Actus X for cloud environments, improving resource efficiency and helping customers control infrastructure costs. Actus X continues to support on-premises, cloud-native and hybrid architectures, so organizations can choose and evolve the model that fits their operational, technical, security and regulatory needs.

Direct connection between content acquisition and monitoring 

At IBC2026, Actus will also present its roadmap for deeper integration with LiveU native LRT, led by planned native support for LiveU Reliable Transport (LRT™) within Actus X. This will allow LiveU feeds to be ingested directly into Actus X benefiting from all Actus monitoring and AI capabilities, without first converting them to another protocol – reducing latency, eliminating unnecessary points of failure, and preserving original video quality, and LRT's bonding and error-resilience advantages throughout the workflow. For customers, that means fewer gateway components and a more direct connection between content acquisition and monitoring.

A User Experience Designed Around Every Workflow

One of the most significant developments is a completely redesigned interface structured around specific operational roles. Instead of showing every user the same screens, Actus X provides focused workspaces for broadcast engineers, technical operators, compliance teams, production staff and media intelligence professionals – each with immediate access to the tools, data and alerts most relevant to their responsibilities.

For engineers, a dedicated technical workspace brings critical information onto a single screen, with multiple channels and delivery points viewable simultaneously to help teams identify anomalies, investigate their source and respond before viewers are affected – a cleaner experience and a faster route from detection to resolution.

"The Contractor Portal changes where SkyOS sits within the construction software ecosystem," said Brian Nichols, Founder and CEO of Sky Systemz. "We've built technology that helps suppliers simplify how they operate, get paid and manage their businesses. Now we're extending that experience to the companies they serve. By connecting both sides of the transaction, we can remove friction for the customer while giving the supplier greater visibility, control and efficiency."

Connecting Both Sides of the Construction Transaction

The Contractor Portal is designed specifically for the account-based relationships common across ready mix, asphalt, aggregates and the broader construction industry.

Rather than introducing another disconnected payment system, the portal works directly with SkyOS. SkyOS remains the system of record for payment status, while payments are securely facilitated through Fractal.

Completed Contractor Portal payments automatically flow back into SkyOS. If a supplier records an offline payment, such as cash or check, the Contractor Portal reflects that the transaction has been paid. Canceled or deleted invoices and payment requests are also updated automatically.

The result is a connected experience on both sides of the transaction: greater self-service and visibility for the customer, with less manual reconciliation and administrative back-and-forth for the supplier.

Key Contractor Portal capabilities include:

  • Centralized payment visibility: Customers can access invoices and payment requests from one account and quickly identify what is outstanding, overdue or complete.
  • Detailed invoice review: Customers can review amounts, dates and line-item details before making a payment.
  • Integrated agreements: When an agreement is required, customers can review and sign it as part of the payment process instead of managing a separate workflow.
  • Card and bank payments powered by Fractal: Payment information is securely handled within the Fractal payment experience.
  • Customer team management: Account administrators can invite team members and manage access, while individual users can be scoped to the transactions relevant to them.
  • Merchant branding: The portal reflects the supplier's branding, keeping the supplier at the center of the customer experience.
  • Automatic SkyOS synchronization: Online payments, offline payments, canceled transactions and deleted transactions remain aligned between the portal and SkyOS.

Expanding the SkyOS Ecosystem

The Contractor Portal also marks a larger strategic step for Sky Systemz as the company expands deeper into the construction value chain.

By creating technology for the businesses purchasing from construction materials suppliers—not only the suppliers themselves—SkyOS creates a new connection between the two sides of the industry's payment ecosystem.

That connection creates opportunities to solve more of the operational fragmentation that exists between suppliers, contractors and their teams as invoices, agreements, payments and financial information move between organizations.

"Our vision for SkyOS has never been to build another isolated piece of software," Nichols added. "The opportunity is to connect the systems, workflows and businesses that keep construction moving. Supporting our customers' customers is a major step in creating value in that connected ecosystem."

The SkyOS Contractor Portal launched today and is now available to customers nationwide.

To learn more or schedule a demonstration of the SkyOS Contractor Portal, visit SkySystemz.com.

About Sky Systemz

Sky Systemz is a Lexington, Kentucky-based financial technology and software company building technology for the construction and heavy building materials industry. Its flagship platform, SkyOS, is a modular operating system designed to simplify complex business operations by connecting payments, customer management, transactions and other essential workflows in one ecosystem.

Through its partnership with Fractal, Sky Systemz is working to modernize construction payments and financial technology while helping businesses reduce complexity, protect margins and create more connected experiences across the industry.

Learn more at SkySystemz.com and follow Sky Systemz on LinkedIn.

About Fractal

Fractal is a financial technology company modernizing how businesses accept, manage and move money. Through secure, integrated payment technology, Fractal helps construction and other complex industries simplify payment workflows, reduce friction and create more connected financial experiences.

Fractal powers payments across the SkyOS ecosystem, giving suppliers and their customers secure ways to complete card and bank transactions within the workflows they already use.

Learn more at FractalPay.com and follow Fractal on LinkedIn.

The company offers integrators top-tier drivers for seamless integration with many of the industry's top control platforms, such as Control4 and Crestron and many others -- coupled with a focused digital sales strategy designed to maximize installer margins and streamline the specification process.

Custom integrators can also outfit the C2 with a fully customizable frame through SKYWORTH's partnership with hydroframes, available in black, silver, gold, white, and walnut, or in any custom pattern or color, with simple one-step installation over the TV's existing bezel.

"From Palette to Pixel: Illuminate Life with Art"

Michael Gleason, Director of Sales, SKYWORTH USA, commented on the significance of the C2 debut, noting: "For years, the Art TV category has required consumers to accept a frustrating compromise: sacrifice visual depth and image quality for a beautiful frame. The industry standard expected buyers to settle for flat, edge-lit QLED panels that function well as ambient art but wash out the moment the lights go down for cinematic viewing.  Our C2 Canvas Art® TV shatters this paradigm by establishing a definitive new standard for Art TVs. Rather than lowering our technical specifications to meet the competition, we integrated the advanced display DNA of our flagship CE1 Canvas Elite™ Art TV into our standard Canvas Art® lineup. The result is a magnificent display that literally leaves the competition in the dust."

SKYWORTH C2 Canvas Art® TV: The New Standard for Masterpiece Displays

While the Canvas Elite™ Art TV remains the no-expense-spared showcase of absolute luxury with the highest specs available, by bringing such elite features as QD-Mini LED technology and the OmniView Matte Screen™ directly to standard Art TVs, the C2 truly transcends its category.

Specs at a Glance:

  • 144Hz refresh rate
  • 400+ full-array local dimming zones
  • 1,000 nits of peak brightness
  • True HDR10+ and Dolby Vision support
  • Built-in subwoofer with Dolby Atmos – no external soundbar required

The result is a hybrid of gallery-ready aesthetic design and high-quality performance. Far from the stripped-down display typical of standard Art TVs, the SKYWORTH C2 Canvas Art® TV is a complete restoration of texture, shadow, and emotion, proving that the modern living room does not have to choose between art and engineering.

C2 Upgrades the Canvas Art® Portfolio

In addition to the new Canvas C2, the Canvas Art® line includes the C1 available in 75-, 55-, and 65-inch models. This comprehensive range ensures custom integrators can offer clients the perfect size for any space while maintaining the signature blend of 4K entertainment and artistic display capabilities that has made the Canvas series a favorite among discerning homeowners.

SKYWORTH will debut the C2 Canvas Art® TV at the CEDIA Expo 2026 (Booth 2923). The new line will be available through SKYWORTH's authorized custom integration dealer network.  Pricing and availability details will be announced at CEDIA.

releases.title: ESI Named ENR's 2026 Intermountain Contractor of the Year
releases.body:
BOISE, Idaho, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When Engineering News-Record named Engineered Structures Inc. (ESI) its 2026 Contractor of the Year for the Intermountain region, the recognition reflected more than the scale of the company's recent projects. It recognized a contractor that has spent decades building a reputation for complex work, strong customer relationships, employee development, and long-term investment in the communities where it operates.

The award covers ESI's work across Idaho, Utah, and Montana—three states where the company has continued to grow while maintaining its roots in the Intermountain West.

For ESI, the recognition is ultimately a reflection of the people behind the projects.

A Regional Contractor with a Growing Reach

ESI's evolution from a regional contractor into one of the nation's larger construction firms has been built on a willingness to take on increasingly complex work without losing sight of the relationships that made that growth possible.

Today, ESI ranks among the nation's largest contractors, placing No. 105 on Engineering News-Record's 2026 Top 400 Contractors list. The company generated more than $850 million in Mountain States revenue in 2025, demonstrating the scale of its presence throughout the region.

That growth has come through a diverse portfolio spanning commercial, education, advanced technology, industrial, mission-critical, and other specialized environments.

But scale alone does not explain the Contractor of the Year recognition.

The award reflects ESI's ability to bring that experience to projects that are helping shape the future of the communities where the company works.

Building Projects That Shape the Region

Some of ESI's most visible recent work demonstrates the range and complexity of that responsibility.

In Boise, ESI is constructing office and parking structures as part of Micron's global headquarters expansion—work connected to one of the largest economic and technological developments in Idaho. The company is also completing major higher-education projects for the College of Western Idaho, including the Health and Science Building, which opened in 2025.

Other projects, such as The Chancery in downtown Boise, demonstrate ESI's role in transforming existing urban environments and contributing to the continued growth of the region's communities. ENR specifically highlighted the Micron expansion, the College of Western Idaho Health and Science Building, and The Chancery among the projects contributing to this year's recognition.

These projects are different in purpose, scale, and complexity. Together, however, they illustrate an important part of ESI's approach: the ability to adapt its expertise to the needs of each customer and each community.

Whether building an educational facility, supporting advanced technology infrastructure, or helping transform a downtown neighborhood, the work carries consequences that extend well beyond the construction site.

Success Starts with People

Behind every project is a workforce capable of delivering it.

That has remained central to ESI's identity as the company has grown. "Everyone Succeeds Together" is ESI's stated purpose, reflecting a belief that long-term success depends on creating an environment where employees, customers, trade partners, and communities can succeed together.

That purpose becomes particularly important as construction projects become more sophisticated and the industry continues to face challenges around workforce development.

ESI has invested in developing employees at every stage of their careers, creating opportunities for people to gain experience in the field, grow into leadership roles, and build careers within the company.

The result is a culture where experience is passed from one generation of employees to the next—helping the company take on more complicated projects while maintaining the knowledge and relationships that have supported its growth.

The ENR recognition is therefore not simply a measure of what ESI has built in the past year. It is also a reflection of the people who have helped build the company itself.

Growing Without Losing Its Roots

As ESI's geographic reach has expanded, its connection to the Intermountain West has remained an important part of its identity.

The company has continued to invest in the communities where its employees live and where its projects are built. That investment can be seen through its work in education, workforce development, charitable giving, and community partnerships.

The approach reflects a broader understanding of what it means to be a contractor in a growing

region.

Construction companies do more than construct buildings. They help create the schools where students learn, the facilities where businesses grow, the infrastructure communities rely on, and the places where people live and work.

ESI's recent portfolio reflects that responsibility. Its projects are helping accommodate population growth, support emerging industries, expand educational opportunities, and create new economic activity across the region.

That combination of growth and investment has become an important part of ESI's continued evolution. The company has grown dramatically from its early days, but its expansion has not changed the principles that have guided it throughout that journey: developing people, building strong relationships, delivering for customers, and investing in the communities it serves.

Being named ENR's 2026 Intermountain Contractor of the Year is recognition of how those principles have translated into results.

From major developments in downtown Boise to new educational facilities and the expansion of one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, ESI is contributing to some of the most significant construction projects in the Intermountain West.

The buildings may be the most visible evidence of that work, but they are only part of the story.

Behind them is an organization capable of bringing together thousands of people, decades of experience, and a shared commitment to building something that lasts.

For ESI, being named ENR's Intermountain Contractor of the Year is recognition of that work—and of the people and communities that make it possible.

BERKELEY, Calif., Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ahead of IBC Show 2026, Eluvio today announced that Cricket Australia has launched Cricket TV, a new direct-to-consumer streaming service built upon Eluvio's Content Fabric and AI Video Intelligence, extending Cricket Australia's live and archival programming to fans beyond its existing broadcast markets across the globe. Cricket TV is now available for early access with full commercial launch of the service expected later this year at https://tv.cricket.com.au.

"We're excited to extend our partnership with Eluvio as we continue to grow Cricket TV and make Australian cricket more accessible to fans around the world," said Dan Allan, Senior Content Manager, Broadcast at Cricket Australia. "Cricket TV brings live matches and some of the best moments from our archive together in one place for fans around the world. Eluvio has been a fantastic partner throughout the process, helping us deliver a high-quality viewing experience while giving us the flexibility to keep evolving the platform. During the early access period, Cricket TV has already reached viewers in more than 40 countries, highlighting the strong global interest in Australian cricket."

"We're honored to have extended our relationship with Cricket Australia, not only to serve their fans with live matches, but also to serve as a model for other sports organizations looking for the most efficient and cost-effective way to deliver protected sports content with the quality today's global viewers deserve," said Michelle Munson, CEO and Co-founder, Eluvio. "With one Fabric, sports rights holders can unlock dark markets and monetize live and VOD and leverage frame-accurate inline AI, without file copies— all at a fraction of legacy costs while retaining full control of their customers' experience and viewer analytics."

A Unified Platform for Streaming and AI Video Intelligence

Cricket TV provides a white-label browser, mobile, and connected TV application to its viewers built using the Eluvio Media Wallet platform (full turnkey OTT Suite). Cricket TV relies on Eluvio's Content Fabric to receive live matches or archival source feeds and dynamically ingests, transcodes, publishes and generates just-in-time streaming output directly to viewers. Streaming is provided at full source resolution, including HD and 4K, with dynamic automatic adaptation to the user's available bandwidth with low latency HLS/DASH delivery, unlimited multi-view, "zero-copy" live-to-VoD and fast DVR playback. The platform also provides subscriptions, pay-per-view, and/or ad-supported monetization, while providing end-to-end content security and anti-piracy protection including strong encryption, DRM, forensic watermarking, and dynamic authorization per-offering including geo blocking and rights control. All features are built-in allowing for a hyper-efficient, tamper-proof distribution, fast and easy purchasing, and on-screen authenticity proofs for the viewer.

In addition, the Eluvio Video Intelligence Editor (EVIE) and AI-assisted tools provide frame-accurate, in-line analysis, indexing, and search, composition, and transformation such as live vertical video, all without file copies or re-transcoding. Finally, Eluvio Content Analytics provides complete transparency of source-to-viewer audience, QoS, and sales analytics. Full details about Eluvio's technical capabilities and benefits can be found at https://eluv.io

Eluvio at IBC Show 2026

During IBC Show 2026 at the RAI Amsterdam, Eluvio will highlight its work with Cricket Australia and showcase the full capabilities of the Content Fabric and Eluvio AI in Hall 8, Stand 8.MS5, and in the Future Tech Zone, Hall 14, Stand 14.A58, September 11–14, 2026. Eluvio's CEO and co-founder, Michelle Munson, will also speak on the Future Tech Zone stage on Sunday, September 13 from 2:00–2:15 p.m. Registration for one-on-one meetings and information about Eluvio's on-site keynote demonstrations at IBC is available at https://ibc.eluv.io.

About Eluvio

Eluvio (https://eluv.io) is solving the generational problems of video over the Internet with its Content Fabric Protocol — transforming the distribution and monetization of premium video and digital media in contrast to legacy cloud workflows and CDNs. Eluvio serves Amazon Studios/MGM, Cricket Australia, European Professional Club Rugby, FOX, SONY, Telstra Broadcast Services, UEFA, United Rugby Championship, Warner Bros., WPALiveTV, WWE, and others. Led by Michelle Munson and Serban Simu, founders and inventors of Aspera, and based in Berkeley, California. Eluvio holds  more than 15 issued US patents and has won multiple NAB Streaming Product of the Year awards, the Seicon Grand Prize, the Hollywood Professional Association Engineering Excellence Award, and other industry honors. On X: @EluvioInc | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/company/eluv-io

About Cricket Australia

Cricket Australia is the national governing body for the sport of cricket in Australia, responsible for the game at the international, domestic, and grassroots levels, including the Australian Men's and Women's national teams and domestic competitions such as the Sheffield Shield, the WNCL, and the KFC BBL and WBBL. More information is available at cricket.com.au.
